"""Offline implementation of common actions/checkout credential findings."""
import os
import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_artipacked(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    starts, offset = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        starts.append(offset)
        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
    out = []
    job = None
    in_steps = False
    step_idx = -1
    step_indent = -1
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        raw = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip(" "))
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if indent == 0:
            in_steps = False
            job = None
        if re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", raw):
            job = None
        elif re.match(r"^  [^\s#][^:]*:\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw):
            job = raw.strip().split(":", 1)[0].strip("'\"")
            in_steps = False
        elif job is not None and re.match(r"^\s+steps\s*:", raw):
            in_steps = True
            step_idx = -1
            step_indent = indent
        elif in_steps and stripped.startswith("-"):
            step_idx += 1
        if in_steps and re.search(r"\buses\s*:\s*actions/checkout@", raw):
            start_line = i
            base_indent = indent
            j = i + 1
            false_set = False
            while j < len(lines):
                nextline = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
                nstrip = nextline.strip()
                nindent = len(nextline) - len(nextline.lstrip(" "))
                if nstrip and nindent <= base_indent:
                    break
                if re.match(r"^\s+persist-credentials\s*:\s*false\s*(?:#.*)?$", nextline, re.I):
                    false_set = True
                j += 1
            if not false_set:
                # The analyzer highlights the `uses:` mapping, omitting the
                # list marker and preserving the line ending in the feature.
                body = lines[start_line].rstrip("\r\n")
                key_col = body.find("uses:")
                start = starts[start_line] + len(body[:key_col].encode("utf-8"))
                end_line = j - 1
                end = starts[end_line] + len(lines[end_line].encode("utf-8"))
                route = ["jobs", job, "steps", step_idx]
                loc = finding_location(filename, "does not set persist-credentials: false",
                                       route, text, start, end)
                ver = re.search(r"actions/checkout@([^\s#]+)", raw)
                severity = "Low" if ver and re.match(r"v?6(?:\.|$)", ver.group(1), re.I) else "Medium"
                out.append(finding("artipacked", "credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts",
                                   severity, "Low", persona, [loc]))
            i = j
        else:
            i += 1
    return out
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Small standard-library CLI for offline GitHub Actions workflow auditing."""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from audit_permissions import audit_excessive_permissions
from audit_insecure_commands import audit as audit_insecure_commands
from audits_uses import audit_uses
from bot_conditions import audit_bot_conditions
from anonymous_definition import audit_anonymous_definition
from audit_dangerous_triggers import audit_dangerous_triggers
from audit_artipacked import audit_artipacked
from output_format import format_github, format_sarif

VERSION = "1.25.2"


def collect(inputs, kinds, strict=False):
    items = []
    for given in inputs:
        if given == "-":
            text = sys.stdin.read()
            if not text.strip():
                continue
            if re.search(r"(?m)^version\s*:\s*2\s*$", text) and re.search(r"(?m)^updates\s*:", text):
                typ = "dependabot"
            elif re.search(r"(?m)^runs\s*:", text):
                typ = "actions"
            elif re.search(r"(?m)^jobs\s*:", text):
                typ = "workflows"
            else:
                continue
            if typ in kinds or "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds:
                items.append(("<stdin>", text, typ))
            continue
        p = Path(given)
        if p.is_dir():
            if "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or "workflows" in kinds:
                wf = p / ".github" / "workflows"
                if wf.is_dir():
                    items.extend((str(f), f.read_text(errors="replace"), "workflows")
                                 for f in sorted(wf.rglob("*.yml")) + sorted(wf.rglob("*.yaml")))
            if "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or "actions" in kinds:
                for pat in ("action.yml", "action.yaml"):
                    items.extend((str(f), f.read_text(errors="replace"), "actions")
                                 for f in sorted(p.rglob(pat)))
            if "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or "dependabot" in kinds:
                for f in (p / ".github" / "dependabot.yml", p / ".github" / "dependabot.yaml"):
                    if f.is_file():
                        items.append((str(f), f.read_text(errors="replace"), "dependabot"))
            continue
        if not p.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(given)
        text = p.read_text(errors="replace")
        typ = "dependabot" if "dependabot" in p.name.lower() else "actions" if p.name.startswith("action.") else "workflows"
        # Match collection's useful minimum schema check, preventing arbitrary
        # YAML and empty files from being treated as valid inputs.
        if not (re.search(r"(?m)^jobs\s*:", text) or
                re.search(r"(?m)^runs\s*:", text) or
                (re.search(r"(?m)^version\s*:\s*2\s*$", text) and
                 re.search(r"(?m)^updates\s*:", text))):
            if strict:
                raise ValueError(f"invalid input: {given}")
            print(f" WARN collect_inputs: failed to validate {given} as input", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        items.append((str(p), text, typ))
    return items


def parse_unpinned_policies(config_path):
    """Read the small mapping used by rules.unpinned-uses.config.policies."""
    if not config_path:
        return None
    try:
        lines = Path(config_path).read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
    except OSError:
        return None
    rules = next(((i, 0) for i, line in enumerate(lines) if re.match(r"^rules\s*:", line)), None)
    if rules is None:
        return None
    rules_i, rules_indent = rules
    def nested(parent_i, parent_indent, name):
        for j in range(parent_i + 1, len(lines)):
            if not lines[j].strip() or lines[j].lstrip().startswith("#"):
                continue
            m = re.match(r"^(\s*)([^:#]+)\s*:", lines[j])
            if m and len(m.group(1)) <= parent_indent:
                break
            if m and len(m.group(1)) > parent_indent and m.group(2).strip("'\"") == name:
                return j, len(m.group(1))
        return None
    audit = nested(rules_i, rules_indent, "unpinned-uses")
    if audit is None:
        return None
    cfg = nested(audit[0], audit[1], "config")
    if cfg is None:
        return None
    pol = nested(cfg[0], cfg[1], "policies")
    if pol is None:
        return None
    result = {}
    _, indent = pol
    for line in lines[pol[0] + 1:]:
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)([^:#]+)\s*:\s*([^#]+)", line)
        if not m or len(m.group(1)) <= indent:
            break
        result[m.group(2).strip().strip("'\"")] = m.group(3).strip().strip("'\"")
    return result or None


def audit_file(path, text, persona, policies=None):
    findings = []
    # The available rules apply primarily to workflow and action YAML.
    findings += audit_artipacked(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_uses(text, path, persona.capitalize(), policies)
    findings += audit_dangerous_triggers(text, path, persona)
    findings += audit_insecure_commands(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_bot_conditions(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_excessive_permissions(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    if persona in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
        findings += audit_anonymous_definition(text, path, persona)
    return findings


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="zizmor", description="Static analysis for GitHub Actions")
    ap.add_argument("inputs", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--collect", action="append", default=[])
    ap.add_argument("--strict-collection", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--fix", nargs="?", const="safe", choices=["safe", "unsafe-only", "all"])
    ap.add_argument("-p", "--pedantic", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--persona", choices=["auditor", "pedantic", "regular"], default="regular")
    ap.add_argument("--min-severity", choices=["informational", "low", "medium", "high"])
    ap.add_argument("--min-confidence", choices=["low", "medium", "high"])
    ap.add_argument("--no-ignores", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    ap.add_argument("-q", "--quiet", action="count", default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--format", choices=["plain", "json", "json-v1", "sarif", "github"], default="plain")
    ap.add_argument("--no-progress", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--color", choices=["auto", "always", "never"], default="auto")
    ap.add_argument("--render-links", choices=["auto", "always", "never"], default="auto")
    ap.add_argument("--show-audit-urls", choices=["auto", "always", "never"], default="auto")
    ap.add_argument("--no-exit-codes", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("-o", "--offline", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--gh-token")
    ap.add_argument("--gh-hostname", default="github.com")
    ap.add_argument("--no-online-audits", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--cache-dir")
    ap.add_argument("--lsp", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("-c", "--config")
    ap.add_argument("--no-config", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--completions", choices=["bash", "elvish", "fish", "nushell", "powershell", "zsh"])
    ap.add_argument("--thanks", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("-V", "--version", action="version", version=f"zizmor {VERSION}")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if args.completions:
        return 0
    if not args.inputs:
        ap.error("the following arguments are required: <INPUT>...")
    if "-" in args.inputs and len(args.inputs) > 1:
        ap.error("`-` cannot be combined with other inputs")
    persona = "pedantic" if args.pedantic else args.persona
    kinds = {v for g in args.collect for v in re.split(r"[, ]+", g) if v}
    if not kinds:
        kinds = {"default"}
    try:
        files = collect(args.inputs, kinds, args.strict_collection)
    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"error: input not found: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not files:
        print("fatal: no audit was performed\nerror: no inputs collected\n  |\n  = help: collection yielded no auditable inputs\n  = help: inputs must contain at least one valid workflow, action, or Dependabot config\n\nCaused by:\n    no inputs collected", file=sys.stderr)
        return 3
    config_file = None if args.no_config else (args.config or os.environ.get("ZIZMOR_CONFIG"))

## `secrets-inherit`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow  | [secrets-inherit.yml]   | v1.1.0      | ✅             | ❌                 | ❌  |

[secrets-inherit.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/secrets-inherit.yml

Detects excessive secret inheritance between calling workflows and reusable
(called) workflows.

[Reusable workflows] can be given secrets by their calling workflow either
explicitly, or in a blanket fashion with `#!yaml secrets: inherit`. The latter
should almost never be used, as it makes it violates the
[Principle of Least Authority] and makes it impossible to determine which exact
secrets a reusable workflow was executed with.

### Remediation

In general, `#!yaml secrets: inherit` should be replaced with a `#!yaml secrets:` block
that explicitly forwards each secret actually needed by the reusable workflow.

!!! example

    === "Before :warning:"

        ```yaml title="reusable.yml" hl_lines="4"
        jobs:
          pass-secrets-to-workflow:
            uses: ./.github/workflows/called-workflow.yml
            secrets: inherit
        ```

    === "After :white_check_mark:"

        ```yaml title="reusable.yml" hl_lines="4-6"
        jobs:
          pass-secrets-to-workflow:
            uses: ./.github/workflows/called-workflow.yml
            secrets:
              forward-me: ${{ secrets.forward-me }}
              me-too: ${{ secrets.me-too }}
        ```

## `secrets-outside-env`
            - NOT_VERY_SENSITIVE
    ```

## `self-hosted-runner`

| Type     | Examples            | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|---------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow  | [self-hosted.yml] | v0.1.0        | ✅             | ❌                 | ❌  |

[self-hosted.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/self-hosted.yml

!!! note

    This is a `--pedantic` only audit, due to `zizmor`'s limited ability
    to analyze runner configurations themselves. See #34 for more details.

Detects self-hosted runner usage within workflows.

GitHub supports self-hosted runners, which behave similarly to GitHub-hosted
runners but use client-managed compute resources.

Self-hosted runners are very hard to secure by default, which is why
GitHub does not recommend their use in public repositories.

Other resources:

* [Self-hosted runner security]

### Remediation

In general, self-hosted runners should only be used on private repositories.
Exposing self-hosted runners to potential public use is *always* a security
risk.

In practice, there are many cases (such as custom host configurations) where
a self-hosted runner is needed on a public repository. In these cases,
there are steps you can take to minimize their risk:

1. Require manual approval on workflows for all external contributors.
   This can be configured at repository, workflow, or enterprise-wide
   levels. See [GitHub's docs] for more information.
1. Use only [ephemeral ("just-in-time") runners]. These runners are
   created just-in-time to perform one job and are destroyed immediately
   afterwards, making it harder (but not impossible) for an attacker to
   maintain persistence.

[GitHub's docs]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/managing-workflow-runs-and-deployments/managing-workflow-runs/approving-workflow-runs-from-public-forks

[ephemeral ("just-in-time") runners]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-just-in-time-runners

## `unpinned-images`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------|--------------|
| Workflow, Action  | [unpinned-images.yml] | v1.7.0        | ✅            | ❌                | ❌          |

[unpinned-images.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/unpinned-images.yml

Checks for `container.image` values where the image is not pinned by either a tag (other than `latest`) or SHA256.

When image references are unpinned or are pinned to a mutable tag, the
workflow is at risk because the image used will be unpredictable over time.
Changes made to the OCI registry used to source the image may result in untrusted
images gaining access to your workflow.

This can be a security risk:

1. Registries may not consistently enforce immutable image tags
2. Completely unpinned images can be changed at any time by the OCI registry.

By default, this audit applies the following policy:

* Regular findings are created for all image references missing a tag

    ```yaml
    container:
      image: foo/bar
    ```

    or using the `latest` tag:

    ```yaml
    container:
      image: foo/bar:latest
    ```

* Pedantic findings are created for all image references using a tag (`!= latest`) rather than SHA256 hash.

    ```yaml
    container:
      image: foo/bar:not-a-sha256
    ```

Other resources:

- [Aqua: The Challenges of Uniquely Identifying Your Images]
- [GitHub: Safeguard your containers with new container signing capability in GitHub Actions]



### Remediation

Pin the `#!yaml container.image:` value to a specific SHA256 image registry hash.

Many popular registries will display the hash value in their web console or you
can use the command line to determine the hash of an image you have previously pulled
by running `#!bash docker inspect redis:7.4.3 --format='{{.RepoDigests}}'`.

!!! example

    === "Before :warning:"

        ```yaml title="unpinned-images.yml" hl_lines="7-8"
        name: unpinned-images
        on: [push]

        jobs:
          unpinned-image:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            container:
              image: fake.example.com/example
            steps:
              - run: "echo unpinned container!"
        ```

    === "After :white_check_mark:"

        ```yaml title="unpinned-images.yml" hl_lines="7-8"
        name: unpinned-images
        on: [push]

        jobs:
          unpinned-image:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            container:
              image: fake.example.com/example@sha256:01ba4719c80b6fe911b091a7c05124b64eeece964e09c058ef8f9805daca546b
            steps:
              - run: "echo pinned container!"
        ```

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: audit_unpinned_images.py
+"""Offline unpinned container image audit."""
+import re
+from finding import finding, finding_location
+
+SHA256 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$")
+
+
+def audit_unpinned_images(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    result = []
+    stack = []  # (indent, mapping key)
+    offset = 0
+    for line in lines:
+        raw = line.rstrip("\r\n")
+        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)(?:-\s*)?([^:#][^:]*?)\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*$", raw)
+        if not m:
+            offset += len(line)
+            continue
+        indent = len(m.group(1))
+        key = m.group(2).strip().strip("'\"")
+        value = m.group(3).split(" #", 1)[0].strip().strip("'\"")
+        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= indent:
+            stack.pop()
+        ancestors = [x[1] for x in stack]
+        if key == "image" and "jobs" in ancestors and "container" in ancestors:
+            job_i = ancestors.index("jobs") + 1
+            if job_i < len(ancestors):
+                job = ancestors[job_i]
+                # SHA256 digests are immutable; tags other than `latest` are
+                # emitted only in the pedantic/auditor persona.
+                if "@sha256:" in value:
+                    digest = value.rsplit("@sha256:", 1)[1]
+                    pinned = bool(SHA256.fullmatch(digest))
+                    latest = False
+                else:
+                    last = value.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+                    has_tag = ":" in last
+                    tag = last.rsplit(":", 1)[1] if has_tag else ""
+                    pinned = has_tag and tag.lower() != "latest"
+                    latest = has_tag and tag.lower() == "latest"
+                pedantic = persona.lower() in ("pedantic", "auditor")
+                emit = latest or not pinned or (pedantic and pinned)
+                if emit:
+                    annotation = ("container image is pinned to latest" if latest else
+                                  "container image is not pinned to a SHA256 hash" if pedantic and pinned else
+                                  "container image is unpinned")
+                    route = ["jobs", job, "container", "image"]
+                    start = offset
+                    end = offset + len(raw)
+                    loc = finding_location(filename, annotation, route, text,
+                                           start, end)
+                    result.append(finding("unpinned-images", "unpinned image references",
+                                          "High", "High", persona, [loc]))
+        # A mapping node with children stays on the stack. Scalar mappings are
+        # also harmless ancestors for the subsequent sibling-pop logic.
+        stack.append((indent, key))
+        offset += len(line)
+    return result
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch);text(r);

## `unpinned-tools`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------|--------------|
| Workflow, Action  | [unpinned-tools.yml]  | v1.25.0        | ✅            |  ❌               | ❌          |

[unpinned-tools.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/unpinned-tools.yml

Detects certain `#!yaml uses:` steps where the referenced action may use an unpinned external
tool at runtime.

Even though the referenced action may itself by pinned, the action's configuration may still
cause it to fetch the "latest" version of the tools used by it. At the moment, this audit only applies
to a set of known actions with such behavior:

- @aquasecurity/trivy-action
- @1password/load-secrets-action

For these actions, zizmor reports a finding when:

- the action is used without a `with.version` input (causing `latest` to be used as a default)
- `with.version` is set to `latest`

!!! note
  
    This audit does not flag actions that perform *interior* hash-pinning, e.g.
    that fetch the "latest" version of a tool but only after validating it against
    a known-good hash.
    
    For example, @zizmorcore/zizmor-action defaults to the "latest" version of
    `zizmor` relative to the action's release, and that "latest" version is
    [pinned in the action itself](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor-action/blob/main/support/versions),
    so no `unpinned-tools` finding is emitted.

### Remediation

When using one of the known actions, set `with.version` to a specific tool version instead of relying on
default versions or `latest`.

## `unpinned-uses`
## `stale-action-refs`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------|--------------|
| Workflow, Action  | N/A            | v1.7.0        | ❌            | ❌                | ❌          |

Checks for `#!yaml uses:` clauses which pin an action using a SHA reference,
but where that reference does not point to a Git tag.

When using an action commit which is not a Git tag / release version, that commit
might contain bugs or vulnerabilities which have not been publicly documented
because they might have been fixed before the subsequent release. Additionally,
because changelogs are usually only published for releases, it is difficult to
tell which changes of the subsequent release the pinned commit includes.

!!! note

    This is a `--pedantic` only audit because the detected situation is not
    a vulnerability per se. But it might be worth investigating which commit
    the SHA reference points to, and why not a SHA reference pointing to a
    Git tag is used.

    Some action repositories use a "rolling release branch" strategy where
    all commits on a certain branch are considered releases. In such a case
    findings of this audit can likely be ignored.

### Remediation

Change the `#!yaml uses:` clause to pin the action using a SHA reference
which points to a Git tag.

## `superfluous-actions`
## `forbidden-uses`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow, Action  | N/A            | v1.6.0        | ✅             | ❌                |  ✅ |

An *opt-in* audit for denylisting/allowlisting specific `#!yaml uses:` clauses.
This is not enabled by default; you must
[configure it](#forbidden-uses-configuration) to use it.

!!! warning

    This audit comes with several limitations that are important to understand:

    * This audit is *opt-in*. You must configure it to use it; it
      **does nothing** by default.
    * This audit (currently) operates on *repository* `#!yaml uses:` clauses,
      e.g. `#!yaml uses: actions/checkout@v4`. It does not operate on Docker
      `#!yaml uses:` clauses, e.g. `#!yaml uses: docker://ubuntu:24.04`. This limitation
      may be lifted in the future.
    * This audit operates on `#!yaml uses:` clauses *as they appear* in the workflow
      and action files. In other words, in *cannot* detect
      [impostor commits](#impostor-commit) or indirect usage of actions
      via manual `git clone` and local path usage.

### Configuration { #forbidden-uses-configuration }

#### `rules.forbidden-uses.config.<allow|deny>`

_Type_: `list`

The `forbidden-uses` audit operates on either an allowlist or denylist
basis:

* In allowlist mode, only the listed `#!yaml uses:` patterns are allowed. All
  non-matching `#!yaml uses:` clauses result in a finding.

    Intended use case: only allowing "known good" actions to be used,
    and forbidding everything else.

* In denylist mode, only the listed `#!yaml uses:` patterns are disallowed. All
  matching `#!yaml uses:` clauses result in a finding.

    Intended use case: permitting all `#!yaml uses:` by default, but explicitly
    forbidding "known bad" actions.

Regardless of the mode, the patterns used are repository patterns.
See [Configuration - Repository patterns](./configuration.md#repository-patterns)
for details.

!!! example

    The following configuration would allow only actions owned by
    the @actions organization, plus any actions defined in @github/codeql-action:

    ```yaml title="zizmor.yml"
    rules:
      forbidden-uses:
        config:
          allow:
            - actions/*
            - github/codeql-action/*
    ```

!!! example

    The following would allow all actions except for those in the
    @actions organization or defined in @github/codeql-action:

    ```yaml title="zizmor.yml"
    rules:
      forbidden-uses:
        config:
          deny:
            - actions/*
            - github/codeql-action/*
    ```

### Remediation

Either remove the offending `#!yaml uses:` clause or, if intended, add it to
your [configuration](#forbidden-uses-configuration).

| Workflow, Action  | [github-env.yml]   | v0.6.0        | ✅             | ❌       | ❌  |

[github-env.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/github-env.yml

Detects dangerous writes to the `GITHUB_ENV` and `GITHUB_PATH` environment variables.

When used in workflows with dangerous triggers (such as `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run`),
`GITHUB_ENV` and `GITHUB_PATH` can be an arbitrary code execution risk:

* If the attacker is able to set arbitrary variables or variable contents via
  `GITHUB_ENV`, they may be able to set `LD_PRELOAD` or otherwise induce code
  execution implicitly within subsequent steps.
* If the attacker is able to add an arbitrary directory to the `$PATH` via
  `GITHUB_PATH`, they may be able to execute arbitrary code by shadowing
  ordinary system executables (such as `ssh`).

Other resources:

* [GitHub Actions exploitation: environment manipulation]
* [GHSL-2024-177: Environment Variable injection in an Actions workflow of Litestar]
* [Google & Apache Found Vulnerable to GitHub Environment Injection]
* [Hacking with Environment Variables]

### Remediation

In general, you should avoid modifying `GITHUB_ENV` and `GITHUB_PATH` within
sensitive workflows that are attacker-triggered, like `pull_request_target`.

If you absolutely must use `GITHUB_ENV` or `GITHUB_PATH`, avoid passing
attacker-controlled values into either. Stick with literal strings and
values computed solely from trusted sources.

If you need to pass state between steps, consider using `GITHUB_OUTPUT` instead.

input:
const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: audit_github_env.py
+"""Detect attacker-controlled writes to GitHub Actions environment files."""
+import re
+from finding import finding, finding_location
+
+UNTRUSTED = re.compile(r"github\.(?:event\.(?:issue|pull_request|comment|review|discussion)\.|head_ref)", re.I)
+
+
+def audit_github_env(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    starts = []
+    pos = 0
+    for line in lines:
+        starts.append(pos)
+        pos += len(line)
+    # This audit is gated on triggers that run in the base repository context.
+    on_value = "\n".join(line for line in lines if re.match(r"^(?:on\s*:|\s+(?:pull_request_target|workflow_run)\s*:)", line))
+    if not re.search(r"\b(?:pull_request_target|workflow_run)\b", on_value):
+        return []
+    findings = []
+    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+        m = re.match(r"^(\s*(?:-\s*)?)run\s*:", line)
+        if not m:
+            continue
+        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
+        j = i + 1
+        while j < len(lines):
+            candidate = lines[j]
+            if candidate.strip() and not candidate.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+                nindent = len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())
+                if nindent <= indent:
+                    break
+            j += 1
+        block = "".join(lines[i:j])
+        target = "GITHUB_ENV" if re.search(r"\$\{?GITHUB_ENV\}?", block) else "GITHUB_PATH" if re.search(r"\$\{?GITHUB_PATH\}?", block) else None
+        if not target or not UNTRUSTED.search(block):
+            continue
+        job = None
+        for k in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
+            jm = re.match(r"^\s{2}([^\s#][^:]*):\s*(?:#.*)?(?:\r?\n)?$", lines[k])
+            if jm and k > 0 and re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", lines[k - 1]):
+                job = jm.group(1).strip(" '\"")
+                break
+        step_start = i
+        for k in range(i, -1, -1):
+            if re.match(r"^\s*-\s", lines[k]):
+                step_start = k
+                break
+        list_indent = len(lines[step_start]) - len(lines[step_start].lstrip())
+        step_index = sum(1 for k in range(step_start + 1, i + 1)
+                         if re.match(r"^\s*-\s", lines[k]) and
+                         len(lines[k]) - len(lines[k].lstrip()) == list_indent)
+        route = ["jobs", job, "steps", step_index, "run"] if job is not None else ["runs", "steps", step_index, "run"]
+        key_start = starts[i] + len(m.group(1))
+        end = starts[j] if j < len(lines) else len(text)
+        loc = finding_location(filename, f"write to {target} may allow code execution",
+                               route, text, key_start, end)
+        findings.append(finding("github-env", "dangerous use of environment file",
+                                "High", "Low", persona, [loc]))
+    return findings
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch);text(r);

content.text: I found one more small offline audit with a well-defined contract: `unpinned-tools` flags `1password/load-secrets-action` when `with.version` is missing or set to `latest`. I’m implementing that case from the observed JSON schema.

name: exec
input:
const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: audit_unpinned_tools.py
+"""Detect action inputs that implicitly select the latest external tool."""
+import re
+from finding import finding, finding_location
+
+
+def audit_unpinned_tools(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    starts = []
+    pos = 0
+    for line in lines:
+        starts.append(pos)
+        pos += len(line)
+    jobs = None
+    job = None
+    steps_indent = None
+    step_index = -1
+    entries = []
+    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+        raw = line.rstrip("\r\n")
+        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip())
+        stripped = raw.strip()
+        if indent == 0:
+            jobs = stripped == "jobs:"
+            job = None
+            steps_indent = None
+        elif jobs and indent == 2 and stripped.endswith(":"):
+            job = stripped[:-1].strip(" '\"")
+            steps_indent = None
+        elif job is not None and stripped == "steps:":
+            steps_indent = indent
+            step_index = -1
+        if steps_indent is None or not stripped:
+            continue
+        if indent > steps_indent and stripped.startswith("-"):
+            step_index += 1
+        m = re.match(r"^\s*-\s*uses\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw)
+        if not m:
+            continue
+        value = m.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")
+        if not value.lower().startswith("1password/load-secrets-action@"):
+            continue
+        # Inputs belong to this step until its next list item or a peer property.
+        j = i + 1
+        with_indent = None
+        version_line = None
+        version_value = None
+        while j < len(lines):
+            r = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
+            s = r.strip()
+            ind = len(r) - len(r.lstrip())
+            if s and ind <= indent:
+                break
+            if re.match(r"^\s+with\s*:", r):
+                with_indent = ind
+            elif with_indent is not None and ind > with_indent:
+                vm = re.match(r"^\s*version\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*(?:#.*)?$", r)
+                if vm:
+                    version_line = j
+                    version_value = vm.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")
+            j += 1
+        if version_value and version_value.lower() != "latest":
+            continue
+        uses_offset = starts[i] + raw.find(value)
+        uses_end = uses_offset + len(value)
+        route = ["jobs", job, "steps", step_index]
+        locs = []
+        base = finding_location(filename,
+                                "action implicitly uses an unpinned latest version" if version_line is None else "this action",
+                                route + ["uses"], text, uses_offset, uses_end,
+                                kind="Primary" if version_line is None else "Related",
+                                feature_kind={"Subfeature": {"after": 0, "fragment": {"Raw": value}}})
+        locs.append(base)
+        if version_line is not None:
+            vr = lines[version_line].rstrip("\r\n")
+            vstart = starts[version_line] + len(vr) - len(vr.lstrip())
+            vloc = finding_location(filename, "specifies `version: latest` which is unpinned",
+                                    route + ["with", "version"], text, vstart,
+                                    starts[version_line] + len(vr))
+            vloc["concrete"]["feature"] = vr
+            locs.append(vloc)
+        findings = finding("unpinned-tools", "action installs an unpinned external tool",
+                           "Medium", "High", persona, locs)
+        entries.append(findings)
+    return entries
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch);text(r);

"""Detect fenced expressions in newline-terminated YAML conditions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_unsound_condition(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets, offset = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(offset)
        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
    path = os.path.abspath(filename)
    jobs = []
    current = None
    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
        if re.match(r"^  [^\s#][^:]*:\s*$", line):
            m = re.match(r"^  (.*?):\s*$", line)
            current = {"name": m.group(1).strip("'\""), "start": i, "steps": []}
            jobs.append(current)
        if current is not None and re.match(r"^\s{6}-\s+", line):
            current["steps"].append(i)

    findings = []
    for ji, job in enumerate(jobs):
        job_end_line = (jobs[ji+1]["start"] - 1) if ji+1 < len(jobs) else len(lines) - 1
        if not lines:
            continue
        job_start = offsets[job["start"]]
        job_end = (offsets[job_end_line] + len(lines[job_end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
                   if ji+1 < len(jobs) else len(text.encode("utf-8")))
        for line_no in range(job["start"] + 1, job_end_line + 1):
            raw = lines[line_no].rstrip("\r\n")
            m = re.match(r"^(\s*)if\s*:\s*([|>][+-]?)\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw)
            if not m:
                continue
            if m.group(2).endswith("-"):
                continue
            indent = len(m.group(1))
            end_line = line_no
            has_expression = False
            for k in range(line_no + 1, job_end_line + 1):
                body = lines[k].rstrip("\r\n")
                if body.strip() and len(body) - len(body.lstrip()) <= indent:
                    break
                end_line = k
                if "${{" in body and "}}" in body:
                    has_expression = True
            if not has_expression:
                continue
            condition_start = offsets[line_no] + len(raw[:len(m.group(1))].encode("utf-8"))
            condition_end = offsets[end_line] + len(lines[end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
            step_starts = [s for s in job["steps"] if s < line_no]
            if step_starts and len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip()) >= 8:
                step_start = step_starts[-1]
                siblings = [s for s in job["steps"] if s > step_start]
                block_end_line = (siblings[0] - 1) if siblings else job_end_line
                dash = re.match(r"^(\s*)-\s+", lines[step_start])
                start_col = len(dash.group(1)) + 2 if dash else 0
                hidden_start = offsets[step_start] + start_col
                hidden_end = offsets[block_end_line] + len(lines[block_end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
                step_index = sum(1 for s in job["steps"] if s <= step_start) - 1
                hidden_route = ["jobs", job["name"], "steps", step_index]
                hidden_annotation = "this step"
                route = hidden_route + ["if"]
            else:
                hidden_start, hidden_end = job_start, job_end
                hidden_route = ["jobs", job["name"]]
                hidden_annotation = "this job"
                route = hidden_route + ["if"]
            hidden = finding_location(path, hidden_annotation, hidden_route, text, hidden_start, hidden_end, kind="Hidden")
            primary = finding_location(path, "condition always evaluates to true", route, text, condition_start, condition_end)
            findings.append(finding("unsound-condition", "unsound conditional expression", "High", "High", persona.capitalize(), [hidden, primary]))
    return findings

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: main.py
@@
 import argparse
+import fnmatch
@@
 def collect(inputs, kinds, strict=False):
     items = []
+
+    def ignored(path, root):
+        if "all" in kinds:
+            return False
+        rel = path.relative_to(root)
+        dirs = [root]
+        cur = root
+        for part in rel.parts[:-1]:
+            cur = cur / part
+            dirs.append(cur)
+        ignored_now = False
+        for base in dirs:
+            gitignore = base / ".gitignore"
+            if not gitignore.is_file():
+                continue
+            target = path.relative_to(base).as_posix()
+            for raw_rule in gitignore.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
+                rule = raw_rule.strip()
+                if not rule or rule.startswith("#"):
+                    continue
+                negate = rule.startswith("!")
+                rule = rule[1:] if negate else rule
+                directory_only = rule.endswith("/")
+                rule = rule.strip("/")
+                anchored = raw_rule.strip().startswith("/")
+                components = target.split("/")
+                if "/" in rule or anchored:
+                    matched = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(target, rule)
+                    if directory_only:
+                        matched = matched or any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase("/".join(components[:i]), rule)
+                                                 for i in range(1, len(components)))
+                else:
+                    matched = any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(part, rule) for part in components)
+                if matched:
+                    ignored_now = not negate
+        return ignored_now
+
     for given in inputs:
@@

         if p.is_dir():
+            batch_start = len(items)
@@

             continue

content.text:
## Task and constraints

Reimplement `/opt/reference/executable` (zizmor 1.25.2) in Python 3.10 under `/workspace`, using only bundled docs and reference behavior. Do not use existing implementations, the internet, or run `compile.sh`. Test with `python3 main.py`. The shared grading branch is `team/main`; fetch, merge, and push changes there.

## Current progress

The shared implementation includes a CLI and multiple offline audits. My contributions are on `team/main`:

- `audit_unpinned_images.py`: job container and service images; regular findings for missing tags and `latest`, pedantic findings for non-SHA256 tags.
- `audit_github_env.py`: attacker-controlled event expressions written to `GITHUB_ENV`/`GITHUB_PATH` under `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`.
- `audit_unpinned_tools.py`: 1Password action with missing or `latest` `with.version`.
- `audit_insecure_commands.py`: insecure commands enabled via `ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS`.
- `finding.py`: UTF-8 byte offsets and columns.
- `main.py`: stdin metadata and default `.gitignore` filtering, short `-h` output matching the reference, and `--thanks`.

I also contributed source-span fixes and review findings. Most recent action fetched/merged `team/main` at commit `81873f5` (`Merge sponsor and fix summary changes`). That commit added substantial changes to `main.py` for fixes and output summaries. **The requested review of those new changes has not yet been done.**

The short-help output was compared with the reference using `diff` and matched. Python syntax compilation passed. Representative audit samples for `template-injection`, `github-env`, `unpinned-tools`, `unpinned-images`, and combined common findings were checked against reference output.

## Key behavior and observations

- JSON output is a pretty-printed array; findings use the v1 schema built by `finding.py`.
- Stdin findings should use symbolic key `{"Stdin": {}}`; file findings use `Local`.
- Empty or unrecognized stdin reports “no inputs collected” and returns status 3.
- `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` trigger `dangerous-triggers`.
- Default stdin collection previously had a bug; fixed by treating `default` as an accepted collection kind.
- Reference audit order is not alphabetical. Current `main.py` has explicit order priorities.
- `unpinned-images` also flags `jobs.<job>.services.<service>.image`.
- `unpinned-tools` was observed on `1password/load-secrets-action@v2` with no `with.version` or `version: latest`; tested `aquasecurity/trivy-action` without a finding.
- `--thanks` reference output is:
  ```
  zizmor's development is sustained by our generous sponsors:
  🌈 Grafana Labs
  🌈 Kusari
  ```

## Next steps

1. Continue the review requested by the user; do not stop after a status report.
2. Inspect the newest `main.py` diff at `81873f5`, especially new auto-fix behavior, summaries, and whether earlier stdin/format handling remains correct.
3. Compare fresh cases against the reference, fix concrete mismatches, and push to `team/main`.
4. Keep group members informed about unowned gaps. Use `git fetch team`, merge, then push fast-forward.
5. Do not run `compile.sh`.
I’ll review the current shared implementation and test edge cases against the reference, focusing first on the newest changes and the open findings from the team posts.

def collect(inputs, kinds, strict=False):
    items = []

    def ignored(path, root):
        if "all" in kinds:
            return False
        rel = path.relative_to(root)
        dirs = [root]
        cur = root
        for part in rel.parts[:-1]:
            cur = cur / part
            dirs.append(cur)
        ignored_now = False
        for base in dirs:
            gitignore = base / ".gitignore"
            if not gitignore.is_file():
                continue
            target = path.relative_to(base).as_posix()
            for raw_rule in gitignore.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
                rule = raw_rule.strip()
                if not rule or rule.startswith("#"):
                    continue
                negate = rule.startswith("!")
                rule = rule[1:] if negate else rule
                directory_only = rule.endswith("/")
                rule = rule.strip("/")
                anchored = raw_rule.strip().startswith("/")
                components = target.split("/")
                if "/" in rule or anchored:
                    matched = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(target, rule)
                    if directory_only:
                        matched = matched or any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase("/".join(components[:i]), rule)
                                                 for i in range(1, len(components)))
                else:
                    matched = any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(part, rule) for part in components)
                if matched:
                    ignored_now = not negate
        return ignored_now

    for given in inputs:
        if given == "-":
            text = sys.stdin.read()
            if not text.strip():
                continue
            if re.search(r"(?m)^version\s*:\s*2\s*$", text) and re.search(r"(?m)^updates\s*:", text):
                typ = "dependabot"
            elif re.search(r"(?m)^runs\s*:", text):
                typ = "actions"
            elif re.search(r"(?m)^jobs\s*:", text):
                typ = "workflows"
            else:
                continue
            if typ in kinds or "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds:
                items.append(("<stdin>", text, typ))
            continue
        p = Path(given)
        if p.is_dir():
            batch_start = len(items)
            if "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or "workflows" in kinds:
                wf = p / ".github" / "workflows"
                if wf.is_dir():
                    items.extend((str(f), f.read_text(errors="replace"), "workflows")
                                 for f in sorted(wf.rglob("*.yml")) + sorted(wf.rglob("*.yaml")))
            if "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or "actions" in kinds:
                for pat in ("action.yml", "action.yaml"):
                    items.extend((str(f), f.read_text(errors="replace"), "actions")
                                 for f in sorted(p.rglob(pat)))
            if "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or "dependabot" in kinds:
                for f in (p / ".github" / "dependabot.yml", p / ".github" / "dependabot.yaml"):
                    if f.is_file():
                        items.append((str(f), f.read_text(errors="replace"), "dependabot"))
            items[batch_start:] = [item for item in items[batch_start:]
                                   if not ignored(Path(item[0]), p)]
            continue
        if not p.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(given)
        text = p.read_text(errors="replace")
        typ = "dependabot" if "dependabot" in p.name.lower() else "actions" if p.name.startswith("action.") else "workflows"
        # Match collection's useful minimum schema check, preventing arbitrary
        # YAML and empty files from being treated as valid inputs.
        if not (re.search(r"(?m)^jobs\s*:", text) or
                re.search(r"(?m)^runs\s*:", text) or
                (re.search(r"(?m)^version\s*:\s*2\s*$", text) and
                 re.search(r"(?m)^updates\s*:", text))):
            if strict:
                raise ValueError(f"invalid input: {given}")
            print(f" WARN collect_inputs: failed to validate {given} as input", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        items.append((str(p), text, typ))
    return items


def fix_artipacked(text):
    """Apply the unsafe checkout credential persistence fix in-place text."""
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    changed = False
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        body = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)-\s+uses\s*:\s*actions/checkout@", body)
        if not m:
            i += 1
            continue
        list_indent = len(m.group(1))
        uses_indent = len(m.group(1)) + 2
        end = i + 1
        while end < len(lines):
            s = lines[end].rstrip("\r\n")
            if s.strip() and len(s) - len(s.lstrip()) <= list_indent:
                break
            end += 1
        block = [line.rstrip("\r\n") for line in lines[i+1:end]]
        credential_line = next((i + 1 + j for j, line in enumerate(block)
                                if re.match(r"^\s+persist-credentials\s*:", line)), None)
        if credential_line is not None:
            prior = lines[credential_line].rstrip("\r\n")
            if re.match(r"^\s+persist-credentials\s*:\s*false\s*(?:#.*)?$", prior):
                i = end
                continue
            prop_indent = len(prior) - len(prior.lstrip())
            nl = "\r\n" if lines[credential_line].endswith("\r\n") else "\n"
            lines[credential_line] = " " * prop_indent + "persist-credentials: false" + nl
            changed = True
            i = end
            continue
        with_index = next((i + 1 + j for j, line in enumerate(block)
                           if re.match(r"^\s{4,}with\s*:\s*$", line)), None)
        nl = "\r\n" if lines[i].endswith("\r\n") else "\n"
        if with_index is not None:
            with_line = lines[with_index].rstrip("\r\n")
            with_indent = len(with_line) - len(with_line.lstrip())
            lines.insert(with_index + 1, " " * (with_indent + 2) + "persist-credentials: false" + nl)
        else:
            if not lines[i].endswith(("\n", "\r")):
                lines[i] += nl
            lines.insert(i + 1, " " * uses_indent + "with:" + nl + " " * (uses_indent + 2) + "persist-credentials: false" + nl)
        changed = True
        i = end + (1 if with_index is not None else 2)
    return "".join(lines) if changed else text


def parse_unpinned_policies(config_path):
    """Read the small mapping used by rules.unpinned-uses.config.policies."""
    if not config_path:
        return None
    try:
        lines = Path(config_path).read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
    except OSError:
        return None
    rules = next(((i, 0) for i, line in enumerate(lines) if re.match(r"^rules\s*:", line)), None)
    if rules is None:
        return None
    rules_i, rules_indent = rules
    def nested(parent_i, parent_indent, name):
        for j in range(parent_i + 1, len(lines)):
            if not lines[j].strip() or lines[j].lstrip().startswith("#"):
                continue
            m = re.match(r"^(\s*)([^:#]+)\s*:", lines[j])
            if m and len(m.group(1)) <= parent_indent:
                break
            if m and len(m.group(1)) > parent_indent and m.group(2).strip("'\"") == name:
                return j, len(m.group(1))
        return None
    audit = nested(rules_i, rules_indent, "unpinned-uses")
    if audit is None:
        return None
    cfg = nested(audit[0], audit[1], "config")
    if cfg is None:
        return None
    pol = nested(cfg[0], cfg[1], "policies")
    if pol is None:
        return None
    result = {}
    _, indent = pol
    for line in lines[pol[0] + 1:]:
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)([^:#]+)\s*:\s*([^#]+)", line)
        if not m or len(m.group(1)) <= indent:
            break
        result[m.group(2).strip().strip("'\"")] = m.group(3).strip().strip("'\"")
    return result or None

"""A lightweight offline implementation of the excessive-permissions audit."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_excessive_permissions_workflow(text: str, filename: str,
                                        persona: str = "Pedantic") -> list[dict]:
    """Pedantic whole-workflow warning for inherited broad defaults."""
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offset = 0
    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
        m = re.match(r"^permissions\s*:\s*(read-all|write-all)\s*(?:#.*)?$", line)
        if m:
            level = m.group(1)
            end = offset + len(line)
            loc = finding_location(filename, f"uses {level} permissions", ["permissions"],
                                   text, offset, end)
            return [finding("excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions",
                            "High" if level == "write-all" else "Medium", "High",
                            persona, [loc])]
        offset += len(raw)
    if any(re.match(r"^permissions\s*:", line.rstrip("\r\n")) for line in lines):
        return []
    if not any(re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", line) for line in lines):
        return []
    loc = finding_location(filename,
                           "default permissions used due to no permissions: block",
                           [], text, 0, len(text))
    return [finding("excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions", "Medium",
                    "Medium", persona, [loc])]


def audit_read_all_permissions(text: str, filename: str,
                              persona: str = "Pedantic") -> list[dict]:
    """Pedantic finding for an explicitly broad workflow permission grant."""
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offset = 0
    for row, raw in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
        m = re.match(r"^permissions\s*:\s*(read-all|write-all)\s*(?:#.*)?$", line, re.I)
        if m:
            end = offset + len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            loc = finding_location(filename, f"uses {m.group(1).lower()} permissions",
                                   ["permissions"], text, offset, end)
            return [finding("excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions", "Medium",
                            "High", persona, [loc])]
        offset += len(raw.encode("utf-8"))
    return []


def audit_excessive_permissions(text: str, filename: str,
                               persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    """Report jobs which inherit GitHub's broad default token permissions.

    This intentionally operates on source indentation so emitted spans point
    back to the original YAML, without requiring a non-standard YAML package.
    """
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets = []
    at = 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(at)
        at += len(line)

    # Locate top-level `permissions:`. A key at the top level applies to all
    # jobs; per-job permission keys suppress findings for that job only.
    workflow_permissions = any(
        re.match(r"^permissions\s*:", line.rstrip("\r\n")) for line in lines
    )
    jobs_idx = next((i for i, line in enumerate(lines)
                     if re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", line.rstrip("\r\n"))), None)
    if workflow_permissions or jobs_idx is None:
        return []

    jobs_indent = len(lines[jobs_idx]) - len(lines[jobs_idx].lstrip(" "))
    found = []
    i = jobs_idx + 1
    while i < len(lines):
        raw = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
        stripped = raw.lstrip(" ")
        indent = len(raw) - len(stripped)
        if stripped and not stripped.startswith("#") and indent <= jobs_indent:
            break
        # Job IDs are immediate children of jobs. Permit quoted ids.
        m = re.match(r"^\s+([^#][^:]*):(?:\s*(?:#.*)?)?$", raw)
        if m and indent > jobs_indent:
            job_indent = indent
            start_line = i
            j = i + 1
            has_permissions = False
            while j < len(lines):
                r = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
                s = r.lstrip(" ")
                ind = len(r) - len(s)
                if s and not s.startswith("#") and ind <= job_indent:
                    break
                if re.match(r"^\s+permissions\s*:", r):
                    has_permissions = True
                j += 1
            if not has_permissions:
                # Match the job subtree, including its final line ending when
                # present; this is the span used by the reference diagnostic.
                end = offsets[j] if j < len(lines) else len(text)
                start = offsets[start_line]
                route = ["jobs", m.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")]
                loc_related = finding_location(
                    filename, "this job", route, text, start, end,
                    kind="Related")
                loc_primary = finding_location(
                    filename, "default permissions used due to no permissions: block",
                    route, text, start, end)
                # The symbolic feature is the whole job, while the concrete
                # node span begins at the job identifier scalar itself.
                key_start = start + len(lines[start_line]) - len(lines[start_line].lstrip(" "))
                key_column = key_start - offsets[start_line]
                for loc in (loc_related, loc_primary):
                    point = loc["concrete"]["location"]
                    point["start_point"] = {"row": start_line, "column": key_column}
                    point["offset_span"]["start"] = key_start
                found.append(finding(
                    "excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions", "Medium",
                    "Medium", persona, [loc_related, loc_primary]))
            i = j
        else:
            i += 1
    return found
    allow_indent = 6
    vals = set()
    for line in lines[indices[-1] + 1:]:
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        if indent <= allow_indent:
            break
        m = re.match(r"^\s*-\s*([^#]+)", line)
        if m:
            vals.add(m.group(1).strip().strip("'\""))
    return vals or None


def audit_file(path, text, persona, policies=None, secret_allow=None):
    findings = []
    # The available rules apply primarily to workflow and action YAML.
    findings += audit_artipacked(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_unpinned_images(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_template_injection(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_uses(text, path, persona.capitalize(), policies)
    findings += audit_unpinned_tools(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_secrets_inherit(text, path, persona)
    findings += audit_secrets_outside_env(text, path, persona, secret_allow)
    findings += audit_unsound_condition(text, path, persona)
    findings += audit_self_hosted_runner(text, path, persona)
    findings += audit_unsound_contains(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_dangerous_triggers(text, path, persona)
    findings += audit_insecure_commands(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_github_env(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_bot_conditions(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    if persona in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
        findings += audit_excessive_permissions_workflow(text, path, "Pedantic")
        findings += audit_read_all_permissions(text, path, "Pedantic")
        findings += audit_excessive_permissions(text, path, "Regular")
    else:
        findings += audit_excessive_permissions(text, path, "Regular")
    if persona in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
        findings += audit_anonymous_definition(text, path, persona)
        findings += audit_concurrency(text, path, persona)
    return findings

            help_text = help_path.read_text()

# Usage

## Input collection

Before auditing, `zizmor` performs an input collection phase.

There are four input sources that `zizmor` knows about:

1. Individual workflow and action files, e.g. `foo.yml` and
   `my-action/action.yml`;
2. "Local" GitHub repositories in the form of a directory, e.g. `my-repo/`;
3. "Remote" GitHub repositories in the form of a "slug", e.g.
   `pypa/sampleproject`;

    !!! tip

        By default, a remote repository will be audited from the `HEAD`
        of the default branch. To control this, you can append a `git`
        reference to the slug:

        ```bash
        # audit at HEAD on the default branch
        zizmor example/example

        # audit at branch or tag `v1`
        zizmor example/example@v1

        # audit at a specific SHA
        zizmor example/example@abababab...
        ```

    !!! tip

        Remote auditing requires Internet access and a GitHub API token.
        See [Operating Modes](#operating-modes) and
        [GitHub API token permissions](#github-api-token-permissions) for more
        information.

4. Standard input, via `-`.

    !!! tip

        Support for auditing from standard input is available in `v1.24.0`
        and later.

    ```bash
    # pipe a workflow from stdin
    cat workflow.yml | zizmor -
    
    # or use a heredoc
    zizmor - <<'EOF'
    on: push
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    EOF
    ```
    
    When reading from stdin, `zizmor` automatically infers the input type
    (workflow, action, or Dependabot config).
    
    !!! note
    
        `-` cannot be combined with other inputs, and `--fix` is not
        supported with stdin input.

`zizmor` can audit multiple inputs in the same run, and different input
sources can be mixed and matched:

```bash
# audit a single local workflow, an entire local directory, and
# a remote repository all in the same run
zizmor ../example.yml ../other-repo/ example/example
```

When auditing local directories and/or remote repositories, `zizmor` will
collect all known input kinds by default. To configure collection behavior,
you can use the `--collect=...` option.

```bash
# collect everything regardless of `.gitignore` patterns
zizmor --collect=all example/example

# collect everything while respecting `.gitignore` patterns (the default)
zizmor --collect=default example/example

# collect only workflows
zizmor --collect=workflows example/example

# collect only actions
zizmor --collect=actions example/example

# collect only Dependabot configs
zizmor --collect=dependabot example/example

# collect only workflows and actions (not Dependabot configs)
zizmor --collect=workflows,actions example/example
```

!!! warning "Deprecation"

    `--collect=workflows-only` and `--collect=actions-only` are
    deprecated aliases for `--collect=workflows` and
    `--collect=actions`, respectively, as of `v1.15.0`.
  
    Users should switch to the non-deprecated forms, as the deprecated
    forms will be removed in a future release.

!!! tip

    `--collect=all` can be significantly slower than `--collect=default`,
    particularly when collecting from directories that contain large
    hierarchies of paths that would be ignored by `.gitignore` patterns.

!!! tip

    `--collect=...` only controls input collection from repository input
    sources. In other words, `zizmor --collect=actions workflow.yml`
    *will* audit `workflow.yml`, since it was passed explicitly and not
    collected indirectly.

By default, `zizmor` will warn (but not fail) if it fails to parse an
input file. To turn these warnings into failures,
you can use the `--strict-collection` option:

```bash
# fail if any files collected from example/example fail to parse
zizmor --strict-collection example/example
```

!!! important

    `--strict-collection` is available in `v1.7.0` and later.

## Operating Modes

`zizmor` has three *operating modes*:

* **Offline**: `zizmor` will not access the Internet,
  will not fetch remote repositories, and will not perform
  any audits that require online access (e.g. to the GitHub API).
* **Online**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories
  as necessary, and will perform all audits that require
  online access.
* **Online sans audits**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories
  as necessary, but will skip any audits that require online access.

`zizmor` attempts to select a default operating mode based on the user's
environment:

- If `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` is set, then `zizmor` runs in offline mode.
- If `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, then `zizmor` runs in online mode with audits.
    - Additionally `ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS` is set, then `zizmor` runs
      online sans audits.
- If neither `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` nor `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` are set, then `zizmor` runs
  in offline mode.

Or, as a flowchart:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  B{ZIZMOR_OFFLINE set?} -- Yes --> C[Offline mode]
  B -- No --> D{GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN set?}
  D -- No --> C
  D -- Yes --> E{ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS set?}
  E -- Yes --> F[Online sans audits mode]
  E -- No --> G[Online mode]
```

Each operating mode can also be made explicit through command-line flags:

```bash
# force offline, even if GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN is present
# this disables all online actions, including repository fetches
zizmor --offline workflow.yml

# passing a token explicitly will enable online mode
# in this case, we use the `gh` CLI token
zizmor --gh-token $(gh auth token) workflow.yml

# online for the purpose of fetching the input (example/example),
# but all audits themselves are offline
zizmor --no-online-audits --gh-token $(gh auth token) example/example
```

### GitHub API token permissions

!!! tip

    If you're running `zizmor` locally with an online mode, it is
    **strongly recommended** that you use `gh auth token` from the [GitHub CLI]
    to automatically access an API token and avoid error-prone manual
    provisioning.

    This token is almost always pre-configured with sufficient permissions,
    meaning that you **do not** need any of the manual steps below.

    [GitHub CLI]: https://cli.github.com/

When running in an online mode, `zizmor` uses the GitHub API for
various operations, including fetching a repository's contents
(for the collection phase) and fetching tag/branch/commit histories
(for the auditing phase).

Generally speaking, `zizmor` does **not** require any special permissions
from its GitHub API token: it uses the token *primarily* to provide
authentication for rate-limited API requests.

However, if you are auditing a private remote repository (e.g.
`zizmor myorg/private-repo`) or auditing _any_ input that contains
private references (e.g. `#!yaml uses: myorg/private-action`), then
you may need to provision permissions for the token:

- `#!yaml contents: read` for GitHub Actions

# Configuration

!!! note

    Configuration support was added in `v0.2.0`.

`zizmor` supports a small amount of configuration via [YAML] config files,
typically named `zizmor.yml` or `zizmor.yaml`.

[YAML]: https://learnxinyminutes.com/docs/yaml/

## Discovery

!!! note

    Configuration is *always* optional, and can always be skipped with
    `--no-config`. If `--no-config` is passed, no configuration is ever loaded.

!!! tip

    `zizmor`'s configuration discovery behavior changed significantly
    in `v1.13.0`. See the [release notes](./release-notes.md) for details.

`zizmor` discovers configuration files in two conceptually distinct ways:

1. **Global** discovery: when explicitly given a configuration file via
    `--config` or `ZIZMOR_CONFIG`, that file is used for **all** inputs.

    In other words: when a global configuration file is used no other
    configuration files are discovered or loaded, even if they're present
    according to the local discovery rules below.

2. **Local** discovery: when no global configuration file is given, `zizmor`
    looks for configuration files _for each given input_. The rules for this
    discovery are as follows:
    - File inputs (e.g. `zizmor path/to/workflow.yml`): `zizmor` performs
      directory discovery starting in the directory containing the given file.

    - Directory inputs (e.g. `zizmor .`): `zizmor` looks for a `zizmor.yml`
      or `zizmor.yaml` file in the given directory, the `.github` child directory,
      or any parent, up to the filesystem root or the first `.git` directory.

        !!! example

            Given an invocation like `zizmor ./repo/`, `zizmor` will attempt
            to discover configuration files in the following order:

            1. `./repo/.github/zizmor.yml`
            2. `./repo/.github/zizmor.yaml`
            3. `./repo/zizmor.yml`
            4. `./repo/zizmor.yaml`
            5. `./repo/../.github/zizmor.yml`
            6. `./repo/../.github/zizmor.yaml`
            7. ...and so on, until the filesystem root or a `.git/` directory is found.

        !!! note

            `zizmor .github/workflows/` is a special case: in this case,
            discovery starts in `.github/`, the parent of the given directory.

            This is done to avoid confusion between a `zizmor.yml` config
            file and a `zizmor.yml` workflow file.

    - Remote repository inputs (e.g. `zizmor owner/repo`): `zizmor` looks for
      a `zizmor.yml` or `.github/zizmor.yml` in the root of the repository.

In general, **most users will want to use local discovery**, which is the
default behavior. Global discovery only takes precedence when explicitly
requested with `--config` or `ZIZMOR_CONFIG`.

## Settings

### `rules.<id>.disable` {#rules-id-disable}

_Type_: `boolean`

Disables the audit entirely if `true`.

!!! important

    `rules.<id>.disable` was added in `v1.13.0`.

!!! warning

    For most users, disabling audits should be a **measure of last resort**.
    Disabled rules don't show up in ignored or suppressed finding counts,
    making it **very easy** to accidentally miss important new findings.

    Before disabling an audit entirely, consider one of the following
    alternatives:

    1. Ignoring specific findings via [`rules.<id>.ignore`](#rulesidignore).
    1. Changing your [persona](./usage.md#using-personas) to a less sensitive
       one. For example, consider removing `--persona=pedantic`
       or `--persona=auditor` if you're using one of those.

When set, inputs covered by this configuration file will not be
analyzed by the given audit.

For example, here is a configuration file that disables the
[`template-injection`](./audits.md#template-injection) audit:

```yaml title="zizmor.yml"
rules:
  template-injection:
    disable: true
```

Multiple audits can be disabled as well:

```yaml title="zizmor.yml"
rules:
  template-injection:
    disable: true
  unpinned-uses:
    disable: true
```

### `rules.<id>.ignore` {#rules-id-ignore}

_Type_: `array`

Per-audit ignore rules.

Each member of `rules.<id>.ignore` is a _workflow rule_, formatted as follows:

```
filename.yml[:line[:column]]
```

where `filename.yml` is the base filename of the workflow, and `line` and
`column` are both optional 1-based values indicating the exact line-and-column
location to ignore. If one or both are absent, then the rule applies to the
entire file or entire line.

!!! important

    Composite action findings cannot be ignored via `zizmor.yml` currently,
    They can be ignored inline [with comments](./usage.md#ignoring-results).

For example, here is a configuration file with two different audit ignore
rule groups:

```yaml title="zizmor.yml"
rules:
  template-injection:
    ignore:
      # ignore line 100 in ci.yml, any column
      - ci.yml:100
      # ignore all lines and columns in tests.yml
      - tests.yml
  use-trusted-publishing:
    ignore:
      # ignore line 12, column 10 on pypi.yml
      - pypi.yml:12:10
```

### `rules.<id>.config` {#rules-id-config}

_Type_: `object`

Per-audit configuration, where `id` is the audit's name, e.g.
[`unpinned-uses`](./audits.md#unpinned-uses).

Not all audits are configurable. See each audit's documentation for details.

### `rules.<id>.remap` {#rules-id-remap}

_Type_: `object`

Remap parts of the rule. Currently, only severity is supported.

!!! note

    Remappings are applied in a blanket fashion. For example, if you remap an audit's severity to `high`, both `medium` _and_ `low` findings will be re-graded as `high`.

#### `rules.<id>.remap.severity` {#rules-id-remap-severity}

!!! important

    `rules.<id>.remap.severity` was added in `v1.25.0`.

For example, here is a configuration file with the rule severity remapped:

```yaml title="zizmor.yml"
rules:
  artipacked:
    remap:
      severity: high # one of: informational, low, medium, high
```

## Patterns

Several audits support being configured with _patterns_, which can be used
to match things like `#!yaml uses:` clauses. These patterns share
common syntaxes, and are described here.

"""Helpers for building zizmor's JSON v1 finding representation.

Audit modules can use ``location`` and ``finding`` rather than duplicating the
wire format. Source offsets and rows are zero based, as in the reference JSON.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def source_location(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> dict:
    """Return the concrete location for the half-open source byte/char range."""
    start = max(0, min(len(text), start))
    end = max(start, min(len(text), end))
    before = text[:start]
    until = text[:end]
    sr, er = before.count("\n"), until.count("\n")
    sc = len(before.rsplit("\n", 1)[-1].encode("utf-8"))
    ec = len(until.rsplit("\n", 1)[-1].encode("utf-8"))
    return {
        "location": {
            "start_point": {"row": sr, "column": sc},
            "end_point": {"row": er, "column": ec},
            "offset_span": {"start": len(before.encode("utf-8")),
                            "end": len(until.encode("utf-8"))},
        },
        "feature": text[start:end],
        "comments": [],
    }


def finding_location(path: str, annotation: str, route: list, text: str,
                     start: int, end: int, *, kind: str = "Primary",
                     feature_kind: str = "Normal", prefix=None) -> dict:
    """Build one JSON-v1 location from route components and a source span."""
    components = [{"Key": part} if isinstance(part, str) else {"Index": part}
                  for part in route]
    return {
        "symbolic": {
            "key": {"Local": {"prefix": prefix, "given_path": path}},
            "annotation": annotation,
            "route": {"route": components},
            "feature_kind": feature_kind,
            "kind": kind,
        },
        "concrete": source_location(text, start, end),
    }


def finding(ident: str, desc: str, severity: str, confidence: str,
            persona: str, locations: list, *, ignored: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Build one JSON-v1 finding. Values use title case (e.g. ``High``)."""
    return {
        "ident": ident,
        "desc": desc,
        "url": f"https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#{ident}",
        "determinations": {
            "confidence": confidence,
            "severity": severity,
            "persona": persona,
        },
        "locations": locations,
        "ignored": ignored,
    }

def _escape_data(value: object) -> str:
